programme.title: At the end it's the sea
programme.desc: François Pécheux travels the longest river in France, the Loire, from the Mont Gerbier-de-Jonc, in Ardèche, to the estuary of Saint-Nazaire, where it flows into the Atlantic Ocean. 1,000 km down on a fierce and always unpredictable beauty. The globe-trotter meets enthusiastic guardian angels, solitary freshwater sailors but also well-drained characters and lovers of the Loire River. The journey begins at the foot of thousands of thousand-year-old volcanoes of the Central Massif, where we follow shy balloon meanders. Then the river widens to canoe.

programme.title: Trains like the others
programme.desc: In Belgium, Philippe Gougler travels one of the most dense railway networks in the world, passing through Namur, Brussels, Antwerp and the North Sea coast.

programme.title: Hot potato! Potato in danger
programme.desc: France is not only a major potato consumer, cooked in all its forms, but also the world's largest exporter. Focusing on the Hauts-de-France and Brittany, this potato culture brings with it its lot of problems. Indeed, its production requires a lot of energy and water and damages the soil. France therefore faces a huge challenge, namely to maintain its status as a potato master while taking into account the environmental and economic challenges associated with it.

programme.title: Apocalypse: World War I
programme.desc: The First World War is told by Mathieu Kassovitz through colour images from public or private archives around the world.

programme.title: C policy
programme.desc: Thomas Snegaroff welcomed viewers to decipher the news and tell the story of the time. Around him, for this presidential year, two new faces: Blanche Leridon, essayist and editorial director of the Institut Montaigne, and Raphaël Llorca, associate expert at the Fondation Jean-Jaurès. These two opinion specialists decipher the aspirations, fears and hopes of French and French people during this historic presidential campaign. They are also alongside Thomas to interview intellectuals, witnesses, women and men who question or move society.

programme.sub-title: Create new varieties of fruits and vegetables. How?

programme.title: C in special air
programme.sub-title: Seas War: Who Will Control the World?
programme.desc: Blocking the Strait of Ormuz, exploitation of the seabed, return of nuclear rhetoric: on the surface of the oceans as well as under the seas, a new decisive competition for the balance of the world between the great powers is being played. From the North Atlantic to the China Sea, this survey explores Russian and Chinese ambitions, new underwater technologies and strategies for controlling global trade. How does France try to respond to these threats? Military, scientific, industrial and expert experts shed light on these new power relations.

programme.title: The Spanish flu, the great killer
programme.desc: The story of a deadly pandemic. It all started in 1918 in a military camp in Kansas where 30,000 men trained because America had just joined the war. On 4 March, about 100 soldiers left training. All suffer from the same symptoms: 40 degrees of fever, sourness, headache and a terrible cough. Despite the fulgurance of the epidemic, no measures are taken to limit contagion. The priority is to send 4 million men to the European front. The virus then spreads rapidly on all 5 continents.

programme.title: Everything Will Change : Once upon a time 2054
programme.desc: In 2054 Cherri, Fini and Ben, a girl and two boys in their 20s, shared an apartment in a city governed by screens. Most animal species, forests and oceans have disappeared before they were born. Nature now boils down to vast desert areas, planted with wind turbines or covered with plastic greenhouses, over which a thin uniformly red vegetation still remains. By chance, Ben falls into an old shop on a video and a picture of a beautiful and strange creature: a giraffe. When asked questions, the merchant put him on the trail of a community of scientists. This report tells how, in 2020, while it was still time to act, humanity has given up in the face of climate change and the destruction of living beings.

programme.title: "Hallelujah", Leonard Cohen: Music of our lives
programme.desc: The genesis of Leonard Cohen's most popular title, "Hallelujah", is unique in more than one way. First, because it took him five years to mature the text, whose verses have been rewritten over the drafts. Then because the artist interpreted two versions of it with totally opposite meanings. First put on the closet by Columbia label, which refused to distribute the record, this ballad found the way to success through the covers of Bob Dylan, John Cale and Jeff Buckley, who made it a vibrant and melancholic anthem.

programme.title: The Secret Life of British Gardens
programme.desc: It's the story of an idyllic English country garden located in the Lake District. Chris and Liz, the owners, love their outdoor space and do everything they can to promote wildlife. In spring, the garden is full of life: the orchard is in full bloom, the beds are full of bees and the pond is full of bridal parade tritons. Love is in the air! But the breeding season is short, and time is running out for the gardeners to find partners and start a family. At nightfall, a field mouse ventures right under the nose of the garden predators.

programme.title: The Little Wadrouille
programme.desc: After a professional conference, Franck (Daniel Auteuil), a businessman with romantic ambitions, asked his right-hand man Justine (Sandrine Kiberlain) to organize a special weekend with a woman he barely knew. By giving him a generous sum of money and complete freedom for the preparations, he leaves him to make this getaway unforgettable. Justine, excited by this mission, immediately talks to her companion Albin (Denis Podalydes). The latter, an opportunist, sees it as a chance to earn a little money easily and to improve the lives of their eccentric group of friends. However, an unexpected turnaround is on the horizon: the woman Franck imagines for this weekend is none other than Justine herself. As projects take on a comical and unpredictable turn, Justine must juggle her feelings, professional expectations and the quiproquos that are constantly accumulating. The plot is complicated as Albin, aware of the situation, tries to intervene, transforming this romantic weekend into a veritable whirlwind of adventures and revelations.

programme.title: Nomad of the seas, the ports of call for innovation
programme.desc: The "Nomad of the Seas" is aridly experienced by two months of crossing the Pacific, and is docked at the San Francisco Harbor Yacht. Corentin was joined by Caroline Plutz, a young designer who works in Belgium on the "myco-material", a living material based on mycelium, capable of replacing plastic.

programme.title: America: The New History of the First Men
programme.desc: New archaeological research is questioning all our certainty about the origins of America's settlement: bones reveal that the continent could have been populated more than 20,000 years ago. Indeed, the first human and animal traces date back to the ice age. From the first exhumation of a cave full of tools, which put the chip in the ear of scientists, until the most recent discoveries, this documentary follows the steps of Ciprian Ardelean, a Mexican archaeologist from the University of Zacatecas, to question the dogmas admitted until then.

programme.title: Ireland, between land and sea
programme.desc: Between green pastures, peatlands and crystal clear waters, Ireland is full of splendid panoramas, rough beauty. This documentary takes a look at the different environments of "the island of emerald". In Malin Head, the dizzying cliffs dominate the Atlantic Ocean. The Connemara wilderness contains remains from 6,000 to 10,000 years old. In the southeast of the island, Bannow Bay is a Viking heritage. Finally, the very wild Beara Peninsula has a stunning Atlantic forest, which is being rebuilt.

programme.title: Irish islands, ocean outposts
programme.desc: The northwestern part of Ireland is dotted with wild islands where nature reigns as the mistress. Away from the rest of the world, the archipelago is home to an impressive diversity of wildlife: while birds nest on Toraigh Island and grey seals fight for supremacy on the Inishkea Islands, humpback whales are killed off the Blasket Archipelago. Under harsh climatic conditions, these species must adapt their survival strategies over the seasons.

programme.title: Irish islands, ocean outposts
programme.desc: On the islands of northwestern Ireland, time seems to have stopped: far from the tumult of cities, the bright greenery of pastures invariably melts in the blue of the ocean. Yet the seasons follow each other and are not the same. As the elements unfold in winter, the arrival of spring leaves room for a wet and cottony fog. Therefore, the many species of animals present on the archipelago must constantly adapt to survive. When summer settles, nearly 250,000 seabirds migrate to Rathlin Island to nest on tree-lined cliffs. In autumn, off the Aran Islands, hundreds of pilgrim sharks gather: swimming in concentric circles, they are here engaged in an amazing speed dating.

programme.title: "Werther" at the Opéra Comique

With Pene Pati, Adèle Charvet and Julie Roset, under the direction of Raphaël Pichon.

programme.title: Life acrobat
programme.desc: A trapezist and contortionist who passed through the National Circus School in Berlin, Silke Pan fell sharply in 2007, during a rehearsal with her husband and partner Didier Dvorak. The young woman, who became paraplegic, was driven by iron will and resumed training one year after the accident to get to the highest level in paracyclism. Every day, Didier encourages him to surpass himself. But despite collecting the titles, he misses the circus. Silke then took up his old balancing numbers, now on his own.

programme.desc: Russian cartoonist Victoria Lomasko shares her daily life in the two years following Ukraine's invasion of Ukraine. Engaged in the opposition through her militant graphic work, she would then face between 3 and 10 years in prison for her work. Along with director Anna Moiseenko, she looks back at the conditions for exercising her art in an authoritarian regime, particularly alongside Pussy Riot, and evokes several events of importance that led her to exile in Brussels.

programme.title: Dunkirk
programme.desc: "Dunkerque" plunged us in May 1940, during one of the darkest periods of World War II, while British and allied forces found themselves trapped on Dunkirk beaches, facing a relentless German army. The film revolves around several characters whose trajectories cross this coastal city, highlighting the tragedy of war through interconnected narratives. Tommy (interpreted by Fionn Whitehead), a young British soldier, does everything to survive the chaos surrounding him. He managed to reach the beach, where thousands of soldiers desperately expected an evacuation. However, the rescue operation, nicknamed "Dynamo", is quickly compromised by the shelling of German aviation, making every minute critical for those men waiting on the seashore. On the other side of the Channel, we meet Mr. Dawson (played by Mark Rylance), a civilian who is ready to do anything to help his country. With his son and a friend, he used his fishing boat to participate in the war effort. Navigating through the tumultuous waters of the Channel, he faces unexpected dangers while trying to save as many soldiers as possible. In the skies, the Royal Air Force pilot, Lieutenant Farrier (incarnate by Tom Hardy), entered a fierce air battle against enemy bombers. His bravery and skill are tested as he tries to protect the troops on the ground while making crucial decisions for his own survival.

programme.title: Behind the scenes of history
programme.desc: Known as terrifying war machines, the German U-Bootes dominated the Atlantic throughout the war. Yet the reality behind the national novel is more complex. It is part of the German strategy of restoring the country to its maritime power, after the destruction of its fleet in the aftermath of the First World War. In February 1939 Hitler presented the world with the battleship Bismarck, the flagship of the world fleet. Soon, the submarines of Rear Admiral Karl Dönitz showed their effectiveness, which was superior to the surface vessels of the Kriegsmarine.

After the case was filed by the NGO Platform of European Memory and Consciousness, which brought the cases before the Prague and Weiden courts in Germany, forty-one persons are now under investigation. Among them, three former members of the Politburo of the time. Benefiting from the valuable experience of the German authorities who worked on the deaths of the Berlin Wall, the Czech Republic is thus beginning a long process of memory and justice, which should help the families of the victims to heal their wounds, and the whole country to better understand its past.

The happiness of the couple is short: Alexander suffers from an incurable brain tumor and begins to lose sight. To finance the very expensive surgery that could save him, Marina makes the painful choice to briefly return to prostitution in order to raise the necessary funds...

programme.title: Itinerary of a child soldier
programme.desc: Following the 1986 coup d'état, the northern Uganda was shaken by the violence committed by the Lord's Resistance Army (LRA). The group led by the bloody Joseph Kony was extremely violent and involved the mass abduction of young children, turning them into soldiers. Dominic Ongwen was one of them: he was torn from his family at the age of 9, transformed into a war machine, and in turn became one of the LRA's armed arms, before being brought before the International Criminal Court in 2016. This documentary traces his journey by following Krispus Ayena, the lawyer charged with defending him.

programme.title: In Europe, dry rivers and rivers
programme.desc: This summer, drought caused the flow of rivers and rivers in Europe to drop. The barges on the Rhine were forced to reduce the weight of their cargo, which disrupted the industrial supply chain. How long can the river navigation still hold the shock?

programme.title: Break
programme.desc: Every week, David Chaignon and his team go on the ground to meet passionate people, both in France and abroad. It offers a travelling program that sheds light on the latest cynégetic and fisheries, is interested in techniques in vogue, the regulations in force, new materials...

programme.title: One day in Nuremberg in 1593: The executioner Frantz Schmidt
programme.sub-title: Nuremberg in 1593: The executioner Frantz Schmidt

programme.title: Homo Animalis, a strange species
programme.desc: Among the 7 million or so animal species that inhabit the planet, one of them has its uniqueity: Homo sapiens. But while its senses are limited, compared to those of other animals, how can we explain that this biped with the gripping thumb has spread over the entire earth's surface? In immersion in a campsite - the man willingly letting appear his true nature during the migration of summer holidays -, two naturalists quinquennials will observe a group of individuals to highlight typical behaviors of the species: learning faculties and thirst for knowledge, physical activities, taste for play, social interactions, rituals of seduction.

programme.title: 42, the answer to almost everything
programme.desc: Our senses developed when the Earth was still populated with sword-tedged tigers. While animals hear ultrasound and perceive magnetic or electrical fields, many things escape us. Can the scope of human perception be expanded or does our biological constitution have limits?

programme.title: Kintoa, king of Basque pigs
programme.desc: In the post-war period, there were only a few Kintoa pigs left in the Pyrenees. In the late 1980s, the French butcher Pierre Oteiza saved the species.

programme.title: Guatemala, the guardians of births
programme.desc: In Guatemala, the "comadronas" accompany future mothers, from conception to postpartum. In rural villages, these traditional midwives are often the only health professionals pregnant women can use. They assist more than a third of the country's parturients.

programme.title: Cuisines of the terroir
programme.desc: The Stollen is a brioche bread made from candied fruits and almond paste, and is inseparable from the city of Dresden, where it is part of a centuries-old tradition.

programme.title: Meuh! The horns' epic
programme.sub-title: The Zebu to conquer the arid

programme.title: Meuh! The horns' epic
programme.sub-title: The Yack at the conquest of the summits

programme.title: Jim's novel
programme.desc: Aymeric finds Florence, an ex-girlfriend of the high school, at random of an evening in Saint-Claude, a small town located in the heart of the Jura massif. Six months pregnant and single at the time of these reunions, Florence quickly falls under the charm of this long lost friend. Both of them are engaged in a romantic relationship. When Jim is born, Aymeric is present, just as he will be present when the child takes his first steps or his first school year. Everything turns out on the day that Christophe, Jim's biological father, lands in their lives, depressing after a personal tragedy. Very quickly, Aymeric no longer finds his place in his family...

programme.title: Water keepers
programme.desc: In Nagaland, a northeastern state of India, the inhabitants store monsoon water in rain ponds. These reservoirs allow the land to be irrigated during the dry season at the cost of permanent maintenance.

programme.title: School paths, paths of all dangers
Vatican: The City That Wanted to Become Eternal
programme.desc: How did the tomb of Apostle Peter, on one of the hills of Rome, become the universal seat of Christendom, along with a major political and artistic centre? Scientists and historians trace the fate of the Vatican, which used magnificence to establish its power. Archaeologists search for ancient catacombs and necropolises to reconstruct two thousand years of tumultuous pontifical history, from the origins to the eclipse of the city to Avignon, through the papacy's alliance with Charlemagne to impose Rome in the eighth century against Constantinople.

programme.title: Leonardo da Vinci
programme.desc: The year 1499 marks a turning point in Leonardo da Vinci's career: then 47 years old, the master leaves Milan, to join Florence a few years later. He must honour a prestigious commission: a fresco for the Council of the City Chamber, which staged his rivalry with Michelangelo...

programme.title: Leonardo da Vinci
programme.desc: The year 1499 marks a turning point in Leonardo da Vinci's career: then 47 years old, the master leaves Milan, to join Florence a few years later. He must honour a prestigious commission: a fresco for the Council of the City Chamber, which staged his rivalry with Michelangelo...

programme.title: History of a pact with the Nazis:
programme.desc: In 1936, German writer Klaus Mann, in exile, castigated artists who joined Nazism in a novel inspired by real characters. A review of the genesis of a work that resonates powerfully with the present.

programme.title: Charles Gounod:
programme.desc: Ready to escape old age, Faust sells his soul to the devil in exchange for a new youth and gets seduced by Marguerite. Under the baton of Nathalie Stutzmann, Jonathan Tetelman shines in the title role of Charles Gounod's famous opera, directed by Lotte de Beer.

programme.title: The bottom of the maps
programme.desc: Giorgia Meloni in Italy, Marine Le Pen in France and Alice Weidel in Germany, here are three women who have become emblematic figures of the far right of Europe. Close-up on leaders and parties, heirs of a long political history.

programme.title: Viking myths
programme.desc: Myths are the foundation of our culture. It is all about love, war, betrayal, ambition, the struggle for freedom, sacrifice, happiness, transgression, the place of destiny... After Les Grands Myths, let's discover the mythology of the Far North, which has been a rich source of art history and pop culture.

programme.title: Have a nice trip, comrades! : GDR leaves on cruise
programme.desc: For three decades, East Germany has rewarded its exemplary citizens with prestigious and cheap cruises.

programme.title: When females have power: the matriarchate in the animal world
programme.desc: Elephants are not the only matriarchal animal society: some communities of hyenas, makis, mole rats or suricates are also regulated by females. From Namibia to Madagascar and Tanzania, this planetary round-up challenges the dominant male theorem. These lifestyles, which have been studied more closely by teams of researchers in recent years, reveal other strategies, such as ritualized submission rather than oppression or aggressiveness.

programme.title: Collective Parenthood, a key to evolution
programme.desc: For scientists, human prosocial behaviour – the ability we have to care for others in a disinterested way, and especially through motherhood – could be a key to understanding our evolution. After its birth, a small human is much less self-sufficient than a newborn from other species. He needs a long period of maturation, and needs attention and stimulation that a single person, his mother in the first place, can hardly give him. Archaeological research on funeral practices in the Bronze and Iron Ages revealed the social role of women other than their biological mothers in young children.

programme.title: School paths, paths of all dangers
The museum told by its guardian angels
programme.sub-title: The Gallery of Offices told by its guardian angels
programme.desc: The Gallery of Offices in Florence houses many Renaissance masterpieces. His guards are sorted on the shutter. They reveal here the behind the scenes of their profession.

programme.title: Cuisines of the terroir
programme.desc: The North Finistère coast enjoys a mild and humid climate and has a very fertile silt soil: ideal conditions for market gardening. The Camus de Bretagne is an artichaud big as the fist and well green. Hard, pointed leaves surround its tender heart and fleshy background with hazelnut flavour. The Finistère ocean lands hold many other culinary treasures.

programme.title: Full powers
programme.desc: Luther Whitney (Clint Eastwood) is a modern Arsène Lupin, an elegant thief who is always caught up with the rich. After completing his long career, he began to derail Sullivan's residence, one of the richest men in Washington, who had travelled on business with his young wife, Christy. Everything's going for the best. He gets ready to go back when he discovers that the wall of the vault is a mirror without a tin that looks over the bedroom. On the other side of this mirror, Luther is witnessing a murder involving Christy and Richmond, the President of the United States.

programme.title: Dracula: the true story
programme.desc: Born under the pen of the Irish writer Bram Stoker, Dracula has haunted imaginations for more than a century. But behind the myth lies a Romanian prince who shook Europe in his time: Vlad III, prince of Valachie, also known in his time as Vlad Tepes. Thanks to the recent invention of the printing press, the more or less amplified narratives of its crimes spread to the west of the continent, where they serve as a support for a new imagination that will last for centuries. Together with researchers, this documentary, illustrated with red scenes made in rotoscopy, iconographic representations and animated maps, is part of the traces of the real Dracula.

programme.title: In the land of mice
programme.desc: In search of a new territory, a young mouse leaves her native career. But the danger is on the horizon. After miraculously escaping a hungry owl, she mates with a robust male. Three weeks later a legion of mice was born. Fleeing predators, the valiant single mother of large families must find a cozy nest...

programme.title: Victor Horta's Art Nouveau: A Dream of Glass and Steel
programme.desc: A journey to the heart of the Belle Epoque and Art Nouveau, to discover the most dazzling buildings built by Belgian architect Victor Horta.

programme.title: Festival in the colors of Spain: Concerto d'Aranjuez
programme.desc: To celebrate the New Year, the Orchestre National de France and the conductor Yutaka Sado present Spain through the pages of Rimski-Korsakov, Bizet and María Rodrigo.

programme.title: Irresistible Gary Cooper
programme.desc: The name Gary Cooper is inseparable from the figure of the American hero. His own qualities as a rider served the roles he embodied in western legends. Remarked by Paramount in the mid-20s, he shot under the camera of the greatest directors, with adventure, spying and humanist dramas: Victor Fleming, Frank Capra, Howard Hawks, Robert Aldrich... After Gene Tierney or Billy Wilder, the Kuperberg sisters complete their mosaic of portraits of the Hollywood golden age.

programme.title: The man of the plain
programme.desc: Will Lockhart arrives in Coronado, a town in New Mexico, where he hopes to shed light on the death of his young brother soldier, killed by the Apaches. He is determined to expose those who sell guns to the Indians and punish them. Will soon found that the entire city is owned by Alec Waggoman, a rich breeder who has had to cease to expand his ranch by absorbing the land of his rivals. Kate Canady, the only owner who still dares to resist the latter, hires Will. But he's accused of Waggoman's murder.

programme.title: The Indians in Hollywood, an American tragedy.
programme.desc: Since the beginning of cinema, Indians have been portrayed negatively, thus reinforcing racial prejudice and stereotypes. The Indian is a true figure in the western, perhaps the only one that exists only through this genre. The Amerindians took the floor to tell their story, which was part of the great American history whose film had taken over as a weapon of propaganda.

programme.title: The great moments of music
programme.sub-title: The music of John Williams' films

programme.title: Far right, the new guard
programme.desc: The extreme right has been steadily increasing in recent years, allowing it to rally many young people. Among them, Stanislas Rigault, who has made a way with Eric Zemmour. But he is not the only one to campaign, since Emma, on the other hand, decided to join the National Rally. Finally, Alice Cordier, a young activist, founded a feminist identity collective.

programme.title: DiscussionDoc
programme.desc: In the European elections of 9 June 2024, Jordan Bardella's list of candidates won 26% of the vote in the under-25s. This progress questions the strategy of standardization led by the National Rally and the renewal of its image among young people. What is the characteristic of this new generation of far-right activists?

programme.title: The meeting is open!
programme.sub-title: Housing Renewal: Beginning of Bill Review
programme.desc: On Monday, November 16, MPs began the consideration of the bill to revive and decentralize housing, led by Minister Vincent Jeanbrun. The text, adopted by senators in early summer 2026, includes a number of construction rules that will be relaxed, with the goal of 2 million new or rehabilitated housing by 2030. The bill is also intended to allow the rental of energy coffers by postponing the ban on renting dwellings with DPE F or G. The bill is being discussed in the House.

programme.title: Controversy
programme.desc: Six months before the presidential elections, polls are already everywhere. But do they really measure opinion or do they end up making it? For behind the voting intentions that now speed up political life, there are many critics. Is it not the end of the day that we have to publish polls that influence the voters' choices?

programme.title: Stamp stories
programme.desc: Since 1 January 1849, the Post Office has issued more than 4,600 stamps. From audiovisual archives, paintings and engravings, this collection goes back time with these small thumbnails, as the front door to tell the history of France.

programme.desc: In Franche-Comté, Lyme disease is more severe than elsewhere. Senator Jean-François Longeot is fighting to make this disease known and to speed up research.
programme.desc-more: In Vendée, all the inhabitants realize this: little by little the ocean nibbles the coast. The phenomenon is natural but amplified by global warming. By 2100, 43 000 dwellings could be destroyed in Vendée, caught up in the waters. That is why the Senate Vice-President (LR) Didier Mandelli has made a commitment to this issue.

programme.desc: On Wednesday 18 November, MPs discussed the bill to regain confidence and balance in rental reports at second reading. The text, which was carried out by Socialist MEP Iñaki Echaniz, provides for the extension of the testing of the rents framework in so-called tense areas. If the members do not adopt the text in the version adopted by the senators on October 21, the arrangements for the supervision of rents will be put to a halt before the end of November. The debate is open to Members who wish to extend the procedure until November 2028.

programme.title: The Echoes of History
programme.desc: In the name of the need to win war at all costs, the leaders of France have allowed the military leaders to establish a reign of terror in Algeria.
programme.desc-more: In the name of the reason for the state and the need to win the war at all costs, the leaders of France have allowed the military leaders to establish in Algeria a reign of terror. Although the politicians decided to abandon their power in favour of the army, the army eventually turned against its "masters", until the coup d'état which led to the return of General De Gaulle to power.

programme.title: France - Cambodia, so far, so close
programme.desc: How did Cambodia, marked by genocide, become the host of the 20th Summit of La Francophonie? Back to historical links between Phnom Penh and Paris.
programme.desc-more: How did Cambodia, ravaged less than fifty years ago by one of the most deadly genocides of the twentieth century, become the host of the 20th Summit of La Francophonie? And what remains, more than 160 years after the protectorate chosen by King Norodom I in 1863, of the singular bond between Phnom Penh and Paris? The common history of the two countries is that of a passionate relationship: a protectorate requested rather than impossibly, an independence obtained without confrontation by Norodom Sihanouk in 1953, and then the collapse under Pol Pot's regime. Peace is negotiated in Paris at the 1991 Conference. Those who have lived it from the inside tell behind the scenes. Cambodian officials are talking about reconstruction, the delicate balance between China, Vietnam and the West, and the place France can still hold.

programme.title: Red Army
programme.desc: Created by Trotsky in 1918, victorious for the counter-revolutionaries, and then purged by Stalin, the Red Army is committed against Hitler, who is heavily disabled.
programme.desc-more: A look back at the history of the Red Army, marked by military repression and disasters, but also by remarkable victories. In 1918 Lenin appointed Leon Trotsky to the war station. Whoever has no military experience will prove that he is an out-of-pair organizer. Initially, it was to be an army of volunteers, democratically elected officers. But the number of people hired is not enough. He then launched the general and compulsory mobilisation, supervised by former Tsarist and experienced officers, monitored by political commissioners.

programme.desc: Véronique Béchu, the police commander of the juvenile protection brigade and the Minors Office (OFMIN), is currently in police custody. She is dedicated to the association "e-Enfance", committed against online child crime. From "grooming" to sexual extortion, Véronique Béchu explains the explosion of content through the networking of criminals and the hyperconnection of children.

programme.title: Black Friday
programme.desc: On the evening of the terrorist attack on Bataclan, Daniel Psenny, then journalist at the daily Le Monde, is the author of the only images broadcast and reprinted everywhere, a unique testimony about the terrorist madness of that night on 13 November 2015 in Paris. Ten years later, what became of the survivors we see on the images? Daniel Psenny has conducted a long investigation to identify them. Seven of them agreed to testify to tell their story that night, their physical injuries, their traumas and how they are going today.

programme.title: Red Army

The military prisoners were accused of treason and sent to the gulag. Others lose their balances and plunge into begging. Things change again when Stalin dies.

programme.title: France - Cambodia, so far, so close
programme.desc: How did Cambodia, marked by genocide, become the host of the 20th Summit of La Francophonie? Back to historical links between Phnom Penh and Paris.
programme.desc-more: How did Cambodia, ravaged less than fifty years ago by one of the most deadly genocides of the twentieth century, become the host of the 20th Summit of La Francophonie? And what remains, more than 160 years after the protectorate chosen by King Norodom I in 1863, of the singular bond between Phnom Penh and Paris? The common history of the two countries is that of a passionate relationship: a protectorate requested rather than impossibly, an independence obtained without confrontation by Norodom Sihanouk in 1953, and then the collapse under Pol Pot's regime. Peace is negotiated in Paris at the 1991 Conference. Those who have lived it from the inside tell behind the scenes. Cambodian officials are talking about reconstruction, the delicate balance between China, Vietnam and the West, and the place France can still hold.

programme.title: Who killed the French industry?
programme.desc: For fifty years, France has gradually disindustrialized. Why has the country lost its capacity to produce what it consumes? Investigation.
programme.desc-more: Today, as international crises succeed, France seems to be aware of the importance of resuming its industrial independence. However, the fact is unquestionable: its production capacity is far from meeting consumer demand. This is the result of fifty years of political choices, employers' strategies and societal upheavals that have led to the closure of many factories and mass layoffs. Witnesses, actors and victims of this deindustrialisation, which is necessary, according to some, preventable for others, share their analysis.

programme.title: On the mythical roads of France
programme.sub-title: The Mont Blanc Route with the writer and academician Jean-Christophe Rufin
programme.desc: From Saint-Gervais-les-Bains to Chamonix, this road shows the country of adoption of the writer Jean-Christophe Rufin, who goes to the foot of Mont Blanc.
programme.desc-more: From Saint-Gervais-les-Bains to Chamonix, this high-savoury road reveals the country of adoption of the writer Jean-Christophe Rufin. He went to the foot of Mont Blanc, to the village of Saint Nicolas de Véroce, where he settled for part of the year to write. The multivan journey alongside Nathalie Schhraen-Guirma is punctuated by a stop at Lake Vert of Passy Plaine-Joux, for an "Afghan march", a technique inherited from caravans, as well as by the discovery, near the Houches, of a herd of cows Herens, known for their combative and endearing character. The journey ends in front of the Sea of Ice.

programme.desc: In Corsica, the mountains covered with maquis are home to shepherds and their cattle. The plateaus of the Grand Causses were shaped by the breeders and their animals.
programme.desc-more: In Corsica, under the shepherds' star. In Corsica, the mountains covered with maquis are thrown into the blue Mediterranean Sea. These steep lands with enchanting beauty are those of the Corsican shepherds and their cattle. From generation to generation, these passionate and freedom-loving men have helped shape the landscapes, crafts and gastronomy of the island of beauty. - In the Great Causses, sheep and men. In the south of the Central Massif, the high plateaus of the Grand Causses, rocky and wind-torn, form a sparsely populated territory with a wild appearance. Yet it is the breeders, and their animals, who have been shaping these land of altitude for millennia.

programme.title: Adolfo Kaminsky, the free forger
programme.desc: The fascinating life of Adolfo Kaminsky, a unknown hero who, thanks to his forger skills, saved thousands of Jewish children threatened by deportation.
programme.desc-more: From its first forgeries to protect Jewish children threatened by deportation to its central role in the clandestine struggles for freedom through the Resistance and anti-colonial fighting, Adolfo Kaminsky embodies an intimate and fierce fight against injustice in all its forms. His underground workshop, transformed into a real bastion of freedom, became the scene of his heroic commitment. Animated archives and sequences inspired by ink drawing - a visual tribute to the tool that was his best weapon -, reveal the legacy of an extraordinary man and the journey of a craftsman of courage who marked the great causes of the twentieth century.

programme.title: The Art of Losing in Politics
programme.desc: Failure reveals politicians much more than victory: former Presidents, Prime Ministers and MPs are unfailingly engaged in defeat.
programme.desc-more: From Nicolas Sarkozy to Valérie Pécresse, from François Hollande to Manuel Valls, Jean-François Copé, and Agnès Buzyn and Laurence Rossignol, they agreed for the first time to tell the story of the moments when their destiny is changing. And the next few days: friends who run away, the phone that no longer rings, the desire to disappear. After the night of defeat shock come the days after then the lessons. Some will throw the sponge, others will go through a depression or turn their failure into a future victory. With a unique display-mirror device in which the political personality interviewed looks at the evening images of his defeat, then finds himself facing himself and his reflection, and thanks to the archives of the INA, this documentary raises the veil on a taboo of political life.

The speakers will have a limited and strictly identical time, without interruption, to develop their thesis.

programme.title: QE, the program that increases your Economic Quotient
programme.desc: 80% of French people feel they do not understand economic and financial issues. To help them see more clearly, the economy becomes a game on LCP. Questions staggered, true/false, quotes from more or less exact leaders, interro by Philippe Aghion, the Nobel Prize in Economics: students, supported by business leaders, will play, confront each other, be wrong, learn and debate. Objective: to understand the economy by having fun! For this season 2, we find the main events of the show: "Do not have to have done the ENA", "the Deconometer", "You have the average?", "A True Un False?" and "The Nobel Prize Interro".

programme.title: Polisse
programme.desc: Dive into the brutal effervescence and tearing daily life of the Brigade de Protection des Mineurs in Paris, Polisse unmistakably portrays the fierce fight of police officers facing the worst realities of the flouted childhood. Between the walls of a police station where the loudspeakers of voices and the heavy silences of unsaid people echo, these men and women – Fred (JoeyStarr), impulsive but deeply human, Nadine (Karin Viard), torn between his professional life and his sentimental failures, or Iris (Marina Foïs), whose fragility is hidden under a carapace of professionalism – trying to protect the most vulnerable. Incests, domestic violence, sordid trafficking, forced marriages: every case that lands on their desk is an open wound, a race against the clock to save lives that are already too marked. In the midst of this chaos, Mélissa (Maïwenn), a photographer in search of meaning, is immigrating into their universe for a report. Her external, first clinical, look is rapidly disturbed by the intensity of the drama she discovers, but also by the solidarity and brutal humanity of these cops used by their profession. An attitude arises between her and Fred, as fulcruming as it is improbable, while the brigade's internal tensions explode: nervous laughter to decompress, fierce strife, and this silent anorexia that gnaws Iris, reflecting the exhaustion of an entire team.

programme.title: It's only the truth that matters
programme.desc: The iconic duo Pascal Bataille and Laurent Fontaine offer participants a rare space where words are freed. On the program: true stories, reunions, confessions, second chances... And always this inimitable concept: a curtain, a revelation, a decision. Faced with what their loved ones have never dared to tell them, will the guests agree to join them on the other side of the curtain or will they go on their side?

programme.title: NCIS
programme.desc: NCIS officers are investigating the abduction of a Navy Petty Officer and the disappearance of her husband. Torres is trying to apologize to Abby.
programme.desc-more: In this exciting new season of NCIS, the team of specialized agents, led by the intrepid Leroy Jethro Gibbs (Mark Harmon), finds itself confronted with a series of complex and intriguing cases involving Navy personnel. Their investigation begins with the mysterious disappearance of a man, which occurred six months earlier, and which seems to be a crucial clue to a recent car explosion. As they explore this case, a new mystery arises: the tragic death of a woman whose body was found after a fall of a building. The victim's doctor, reluctant to share information about his or her background, becomes an issue for Gibbs, who must convince him or her to collaborate. Barely this resolved case, Gibbs, accompanied by Palmer (Brian Dietzen) and Quinn (Emily Wickersham), set out at sea to elucidate the murder of a marine, testing their ingenuity and determination. This 14th season promises to be rich in suspense and rebound.

programme.title: NCIS
programme.desc: NCIS is investigating the disappearance of a friend of Reeves's, abducted by strangers. A derogatory photo of McGee is broadcast on social media.
programme.desc-more: Gibbs (Mark Harmon) and McGee (Sean Murray) are still missing after being sent to Paraguay to track down a group of rebels. Two months go by without news, plunging their colleagues into growing concern as they try to find them. Meanwhile, Leon Vance (Rocky Carroll) and Nick Torres (Willer Valderrama) must prepare to testify before Congress about the circumstances of this failed mission. Their concern is dispelled when Gibbs and McGee reappear, but their return is marked by traumas during their journey to South America. Before returning to their duties, they must undergo a psychological assessment to ensure their mental condition. Once the team is assembled, they re-enter the investigations, discovering the body of a missing lieutenant, found in a cemetery by workers. This macabre discovery leads to a new series of investigations that will test the team's skills.

programme.title: Mom, I missed the plane again.
programme.desc: A kid who's been caught up with the wrong plane, lands in New York and leads a hard life to two benethic thugs he had already watched in a previous meeting.
programme.desc-more: In the effervescence of Christmas preparations, the McCallister family is about to go on holiday under the Florida sun, leaving behind the Chicago frimas. But between the suitcases to be closed, the tickets to be checked and the usual agitation of a crowded airport, a crucial detail is not at the attention of all: Kevin (Macaulay Culkin), the turbulent benjamin of the family, was still found alone... And this time, far away from home. The boy accidentally boarded a plane to New York, while his parents, convinced of having him on board, took off to their destination without any doubt. Delivered to himself in Manhattan's urban jungle, Kevin, far from panicking, sees this forced adventure as a golden opportunity. Armed with his ingenuity and disconcerting audacity, he manages to make himself look like an adult, rents a luxurious suite in a palace and even offers the services of a limousine to go to Duncans Toy Chest, a gigantic toy shop where all his childhood dreams seem to be within reach. But Christmas magic also has its shadows: while he savors his freedom found, Kevin crosses the eyes of two faces that ice his blood. Harry (Joe Pesci) and Marv (Daniel Stern), the unlucky burglar duo who had tried to break into his home two years earlier, were once again prowling. This time, they have a deal to settle... And revenge to be met. Kevin's dream is a nightmare: trapped in a huge hotel, hunted down by determined criminals, he'll have to redouble his imagination to escape them. Between wild chases in the halls of the palace, improvised traps and hilarious pros, the young hero will once again prove that intelligence and tricks can overcome the worst troubles. But in a city where everything seems possible, how far will he go to sow his pursuers and find his family? One thing is for sure: this time, the end-of-year celebrations are announced... Explosives.

programme.title: NCIS
programme.desc: The NCIS director, who was kidnapped by Hakim, was trying to pass information on to his agents. He wants to protect his daughter, who might be murdered.
programme.desc-more: Leon Vance (Rocky Carroll), the NCIS director, finds himself in a desperate situation after being abducted by Hakim, a ruthless terrorist. Forced to produce a video in which he supports Afghan fighters, Vance desperately seeks a way to convey a message to his agents. After his release, he has to face the consequences of this traumatic experience while recovering from his injuries. At the same time, Officer Leroy Jethro Gibbs (Mark Harmon) is engaged in a complex investigation into the death of a soldier found sluggish in his jacuzzi, a case that is particularly delicate and enigmatic. As the team tracks a bomb-layer responsible for several attacks, Gibbs, who aspires to a well-deserved vacation, is forced to resume service to capture a fugitive robber. This sixteenth season explores Gibbs' mysterious past in depth, revealing unexpected facets of his history.

programme.title: NCIS
programme.desc: After a quartermaster was found murdered, McGee spent hours on the victim's amateur radio trying to locate a key witness.
programme.desc-more: Gibbs (Mark Harmon) and McGee (Sean Murray) are still missing after being sent to Paraguay to track down a group of rebels. Two months go by without news, plunging their colleagues into growing concern as they try to find them. Meanwhile, Leon Vance (Rocky Carroll) and Nick Torres (Willer Valderrama) must prepare to testify before Congress about the circumstances of this failed mission. Their concern is dispelled when Gibbs and McGee reappear, but their return is marked by traumas during their journey to South America. Before returning to their duties, they must undergo a psychological assessment to ensure their mental condition. Once the team is assembled, they re-enter the investigations, discovering the body of a missing lieutenant, found in a cemetery by workers. This macabre discovery leads to a new series of investigations that will test the team's skills.

programme.title: Taken
programme.desc: A former American intelligence officer learns that his 18-year-old daughter was abducted in the heart of Paris. He immediately began to search for him.
programme.desc-more: In "Taken", Paris' vibrant and often deceptive universe becomes the scene of a haletante hunt. Bryan Mills (Liam Neeson), a former secret agent in Los Angeles, saw his world collapse when he reluctantly agreed to let his 17-year-old daughter, Kim (Maggie Grace), travel to Paris with his best friend, Amanda. Although concerned, Bryan does not know that this idyllic journey will quickly turn into an unimaginable nightmare. Just arrived in Roissy, the two teenage girls crossed the path of a mysterious man, Peter. What begins as a promising adventure takes a dramatic turn when Albanian mafia are calling on young girls and brutally kidnapping them in their apartment. When he learns the bad news, Bryan immediately sets course for France. Determined, he has only four days to find his daughter, taking advantage of all his skills as a secret agent. In a race against time, he must navigate in a dark and dangerous world, where every false step could cost Kim's life.

programme.title: My boy
programme.desc: A man, passionate about his profession and not very busy with his son, learns that he was abducted. He's gonna try to find him.
programme.desc-more: Julien (Guillaume Canet), a globe-trotter journalist passionate about his profession, has always lived between two planes, two reports, two continents. An existence rhythmic by urgency and adrenaline, which ended up consuming his couple. The tensions, repeated absences and wear and tear of time were the reason for her marriage with her ex-wife, leaving behind them a tense relationship, but an unalterable love for their child, a seven-year-old boy, fragile light in their shaken lives. Everything changes during a stopover in France. Between two correspondences, Julien falls on a heartbreaking voice message: his ex-wife, the voice broken by the sobs, announces to him the unthinkable. Their son disappeared during a school bivouac in the mountains, swallowed by the vast wilderness as if he had never existed. The hours pass, the research is organized, but the tracks remain tenuous, and the anguish grows, suffocating. Without hesitation, Julien abandons everything to rush to the place, determined to find his child at all costs. In this mountainous setting where nature, both majestic and hostile, seems to keep its secrets, Julien encounters a wall of silence and uncertainty. The gendarmes, the teachers, the other parents: each has his version of the facts, his doubts, his unsaid. The clues are rare, the hypotheses multiply, and time, an unrelenting enemy, stretches without mercy. Between false leads and disappointed hopes, Julien must also deal with his own demons – his regrets, his guilt for having been a father absent, and this question that eats him up: could he have prevented this tragedy if he had been there?

programme.title: NCIS
programme.desc: As he approached his marriage with McGee, Delilah stressed and found himself in the hospital. NCIS team is investigating the death of an officer aboard a destroyer.
programme.desc-more: In this exciting new season of NCIS, the team of specialized agents, led by the intrepid Leroy Jethro Gibbs (Mark Harmon), finds itself confronted with a series of complex and intriguing cases involving Navy personnel. Their investigation begins with the mysterious disappearance of a man, which occurred six months earlier, and which seems to be a crucial clue to a recent car explosion. As they explore this case, a new mystery arises: the tragic death of a woman whose body was found after a fall of a building. The victim's doctor, reluctant to share information about his or her background, becomes an issue for Gibbs, who must convince him or her to collaborate. Barely this resolved case, Gibbs, accompanied by Palmer (Brian Dietzen) and Quinn (Emily Wickersham), set out at sea to elucidate the murder of a marine, testing their ingenuity and determination. This 14th season promises to be rich in suspense and rebound.

programme.title: NCIS
programme.sub-title: A journey to the end of hell
programme.desc: Two months after Gibbs and McGee disappeared on a mission to Paraguay, their NCIS colleagues refused to abandon the search.
programme.desc-more: Gibbs (Mark Harmon) and McGee (Sean Murray) are still missing after being sent to Paraguay to track down a group of rebels. Two months go by without news, plunging their colleagues into growing concern as they try to find them. Meanwhile, Leon Vance (Rocky Carroll) and Nick Torres (Willer Valderrama) must prepare to testify before Congress about the circumstances of this failed mission. Their concern is dispelled when Gibbs and McGee reappear, but their return is marked by traumas during their journey to South America. Before returning to their duties, they must undergo a psychological assessment to ensure their mental condition. Once the team is assembled, they re-enter the investigations, discovering the body of a missing lieutenant, found in a cemetery by workers. This macabre discovery leads to a new series of investigations that will test the team's skills.

programme.title: Bodin's investigating in Corsica
programme.desc: Christian Bodin sees a murder in Corsica in his dream. But how can we apprehend a criminal who has not yet been de facto? Maria's gonna help him.
programme.desc-more: It all begins when Christian Bodin (Jean-Christian Fraiscinet), after having thought that he saw his father's ghost, discovers a surprising gift: to see in dream the people who will die soon. Among these disturbing visions, one in particular the dreadful ice: the imminent murder of a certain Pasqualini, a clementine producer in Corsica. Neither one nor two, Christian, convinced that he must prevent this crime, decides to take action. Accompanied by his mother, Marie Bodin (Vincent Dubois), as determined as he was fantasistic, he left their farm in Pouziou-les-Trois-Galoches to embark on a lost-body adventure in the island. At the wheel of their mythical Mochet, a car as modest as their budget, the Bodins landed in Corsica with a mission: to save Pasqualini and to break through the secrets surrounding this dark prediction. Their journey leads them first to a local bar, where languages sometimes loosen up a little too much, then to a colorful market, where rumours and anecdotes are heard. It is finally in the footsteps of the clementine producer that they eventually fall, discovering a field of production as picturesque as it is mysterious. But in Corsica, appearances are often misleading, and the Bodins will soon understand that their investigation will not be of any rest. Between local traditions, family rivalries and well-kept secrets, each clue brings them a little closer to the truth... while diving them into situations as bad as unexpected.

programme.title: The Bodin's in Belgians
programme.desc: Maria Bodin and her son Christian are chosen by the Belgian sovereigns to organize a gala in honour of their 25 years of marriage. The duo must learn about the functioning of the Belgian monarchy and be able to live up to this special occasion. Selecting artists in the gala, getting used to princely language, having dinner with an atypical cook and wearing a royal outfit will not be simple tasks.

programme.title: Kaamelott
programme.desc: The island of Brittany, in the fifth century. His legends, battles, the fantastic and respectable adventures of the Knights of the Round Table, gathered around their powerful and magnanimous King Arthur. But looking closer, Arthur is not always as wise as he would like to think, and his dear wife Guinevere is not the erudite nymph related by history, but rather a naive woman who keeps exasperating her husband. Guinevere's father, Leodagan, king of Carmellia, is a warmaniac who only thinks of fighting the other peoples, while his mother, Séli, is an ambitious acariquist always quick to share her bad mood with the kingdom. As for the famous Knights of the Round Table, they are not so brave and philanthropic that we are told that they want to believe it. Perceval and Karadoc are poltrons who are better at making the tavern of the village go bad than in fulfilling the missions entrusted to them by King Arthur. Yvain and Gauvain are two teenagers seeking glory but unable to prove their courage. Bohort is more interested in fashion than in fighting, and Merlin is an enchanter whose spells usually turn against him. King Arthur is embodied by talented Alexandre Astier, who is one of the three creators of the series with Alain Kappauf (Camera Café) and Jean-Yves Robin. He knows how to work with the family, since he shares the screen with Lionnel Astier (Leodagan of Carmelide) and Simon Astier (Yvain), who is the main hero of Hero Corp.

programme.title: The little history of France
programme.desc: In a humorous and offbeat approach, this series highlights characters close to major historical figures of France, such as Vercingetorix, Jeanne d'Arc and Napoleon. Through a series of sketches in various historical contexts, the writers offer an unprecedented look at the landmarks of the past. Each episode plunges the spectator with humour into the daily lives of these iconic figures and their loved ones, often contrasted with the weight of history.

programme.title: Frequenstar
programme.desc: Éric Jean-Jean opens the doors of his apartment to an artist from the French scene for an hour of rhythmic, intimate and totally new television. This season, Fréquenstar breaks the codes of the classic interview and adopts a new rhythm, inspired by the uses of social networks.

programme.title: Kaamelott
programme.desc: The island of Brittany, in the fifth century. His legends, battles, the fantastic and respectable adventures of the Knights of the Round Table, gathered around their powerful and magnanimous King Arthur. But looking closer, Arthur is not always as wise as he would like to think, and his dear wife Guinevere is not the erudite nymph related by history, but rather a naive woman who keeps exasperating her husband. Guinevere's father, Leodagan, king of Carmellia, is a warmaniac who only thinks of fighting the other peoples, while his mother, Séli, is an ambitious acariquist always quick to share her bad mood with the kingdom. As for the famous Knights of the Round Table, they are not so brave and philanthropic that we are told that they want to believe it. Perceval and Karadoc are poltrons who are better at making the tavern of the village go bad than in fulfilling the missions entrusted to them by King Arthur. Yvain and Gauvain are two teenagers seeking glory but unable to prove their courage. Bohort is more interested in fashion than in fighting, and Merlin is an enchanter whose spells usually turn against him. King Arthur is embodied by talented Alexandre Astier, who is one of the three creators of the series with Alain Kappauf (Camera Café) and Jean-Yves Robin. He knows how to work with the family, since he shares the screen with Lionnel Astier (Leodagan of Carmelide) and Simon Astier (Yvain), who is the main hero of Hero Corp.

programme.title: NCIS
programme.desc: Leon Vance (Rocky Carroll), the NCIS director, finds himself in a desperate situation after being abducted by Hakim, a ruthless terrorist. Forced to produce a video in which he supports Afghan fighters, Vance desperately seeks a way to convey a message to his agents. After his release, he has to face the consequences of this traumatic experience while recovering from his injuries. At the same time, Officer Leroy Jethro Gibbs (Mark Harmon) is engaged in a complex investigation into the death of a soldier found sluggish in his jacuzzi, a case that is particularly delicate and enigmatic. As the team tracks a bomb-layer responsible for several attacks, Gibbs, who aspires to a well-deserved vacation, is forced to resume service to capture a fugitive robber. This sixteenth season explores Gibbs' mysterious past in depth, revealing unexpected facets of his history.
programme.desc-more: Within the Naval Criminal Investigative Service, an elite unit specializing in crimes related to the Marines, terrorists or spy networks, a team with a variety of profiles and complementary work in the shadows to unravel intrigues where betrayals, lies and loyalty are met. Led by Leroy Jethro Gibbs (Mark Harmon), a former Marine sniper with a turbulent past and legendary reputation, the agents combine surgical intuition with unconventional methods. With him, Timothy McGee (Sean Murray), a brilliant but sometimes too methodical analyst, and Nick Torres (Willer Valderrama), a former agent infiltrated with explosive charisma, form a duo as effective as unpredictable. Completing the Ellie Bishop team (Emily Wickersham), a specialist in criminal psychology with formidable instincts, Jimmy Palmer (Brian Dietzen), a medical examiner with a heart, and Kasie Hines (Diona Reasonover), an expert in forensics whose analytical intelligence often saves the bet. Not to mention Leon Vance (Rocky Carroll), director of NCIS, whose strategic decisions weigh heavily in the course of investigations, and Alden Parker (Gary Cole), a former FBI profile whose arrival is changing the established dynamics.

programme.title: New York Special Unit
programme.sub-title: No one can ignore the law
programme.desc: In the bustling streets of New York, the Special Unit for Victims, led by the Olivia Benson (Mariska Hargitay) determined, is facing disturbing cases that test their skills and humanity. In this 21st season, inspectors, including the faithful Fin Tutuola (Ice-T) and the insight Kat Tamin (Jamie Gray Hyder), are delving into complex investigations of sexual crimes, child abuse and domestic violence. Each episode reveals the emotional and moral challenges that team members face as they navigate between the pain of victims and the quest for justice. Unity, often confronted with failing systems and prejudices, must also manage its own internal struggles, while striving to restore hope and dignity to the people it serves. The series, rich in drama and tension, offers a free-ranging look at often neglected realities.
programme.desc-more: In the hectic New York City, the Special Police Unit is dedicated to the fight against sexual crimes and cases involving vulnerable victims, orchestrated by the determined detective Olivia Benson (Mariska Hargitay). Each episode plunges investigators into often sordid and complex situations where the discovery of a revolting crime requires their sensitivity and professionalism. The members of this unit, composed of experienced detectives, are engaged in thorough investigations, gathering evidence and interviewing suspects with the aim of bringing the culprits to justice. Cases, including rape, abuse of minors and sexual trafficking, are not only sensitive but also emotionally stressful. The Special Unit would not only act as investigators, but also as support for victims, highlighting their trauma and the challenges they face in rebuilding themselves.

programme.title: Mentalist
programme.desc: With the help of her FBI colleagues, Jane is developing a plan to trap art thieves, who committed a murder in a robbery.
programme.desc-more: After gradually reducing his list of suspects concerning Red John, the serial killer who upset his life, Patrick Jane (Simon Baker) finds himself facing an increasingly complex dilemma. The closer he approaches the identity of the murderer, the more he intensifyes his acts of violence, sowing terror around him. Despite the traps set by Red John, Jane is perceptive and manages to expose the criminal. However, their explosive confrontation forces Jane to flee the country to escape the threat she faces. Two years later, Teresa Lisbon's team (Robin Tunney) was dissolved, and Van Pelt (Amanda Righetti) and Rigsby (Owain Yeoman) began a new life together. As Jane lives under a false identity, a new opportunity presents itself to him, marking the beginning of a season full of tensions and revelations, with the arrival of new characters, including Kim Fischer (Emily Swallow) and the FBI agent, who bring an unexpected dynamic to the plot.

programme.desc: A great information session that combines humour and impertinence. French and international politics, media, culture, sport: all topics are reviewed. Each show has a carte blanche to deal with the news in its own way.

programme.title: Daily, part two

programme.title: Quotidien Daily Show
programme.desc: This program offers a talk show based on current facts. Presented by former Little Journal host Yann Barthès, the show is broadcast in prime time access every day of the week. Between immersive reports, chronicles, interviews, "Quotidien" offers a condensation of the current affairs thanks to columnists such as Jean-Michel Aphatie, Amber Chalumeau, Julien Bellver, Étienne Carbonnier and Pablo Mira. The show also hosts several guests, both French and international. Concerts are even held on the stage.

programme.title: The Flash
programme.desc: A scientist with superpowers decides to travel through time to try to change the past and prevent the occurrence of a terrible tragedy.
programme.desc-more: In Gotham City, a few years after General Zod's defeat, Barry Allen, a.k.a. Flash, was called in an emergency by Bruce Wayne to help him. While Batman is chasing dangerous gangsters, Flash must save babies at risk, while their nursery collapses. Once Barry's mission was accomplished, he heard from his father, accused of killing his mother a few years earlier. Always traumatized by this event, and disturbed by the return to his life of Iris West, of which he was once in love, Flash is thinking of intervening on his own past.

Despite the traps set by Red John, Jane is perceptive and manages to expose the criminal. However, their explosive confrontation forces Jane to flee the country to escape the threat she faces. Two years later, Teresa Lisbon's team (Robin Tunney) was dissolved, and Van Pelt (Amanda Righetti) and Rigsby (Owain Yeoman) began a new life together. As Jane lives under a false identity, a new opportunity presents itself to him, marking the beginning of a season full of tensions and revelations, with the arrival of new characters, including Kim Fischer (Emily Swallow) and the FBI agent, who bring an unexpected dynamic to the plot.

programme.title: 90' Investigations
programme.sub-title: From Valenciennes to Denain: diving into the daily life of the superflics of the North
programme.desc: Valenciennes and Denain mobilise nearly 700 police officers. For more than two months, a team followed the daily work of two emblematic units: the Police-Relief and the Anti-Criminality Brigade. Police officers manage refusals to comply, neighbourhood conflicts, but also marital tensions.
programme.desc-more: Valenciennes and Denain, located a few kilometers from each other, mobilized nearly 700 police officers. For more than two months, a team followed the daily work of two emblematic units: the Police-Relief and the Anti-Criminality Brigade. In Valenciennes, Sébastien, BAC's chief brigadier, manages refusals to comply, which he hates above all else. When a driver refuses to stop, he doesn't let go. He was followed in a spectacular chase against a suspect offender who was actually driving without a licence. But police officers are also facing growing neighbourhood conflicts. Sometimes it is only an exchange of insults, but some situations can degenerate. Marital tensions are also common.

programme.title: 90' Investigations
programme.sub-title: The police of the North under tension
programme.desc: Every day, the 500 officers in Roubaix manage all kinds of conflicts: fighting, rixes between neighbours, burglaries and chase races. This is one of the 20 French cities most affected by crime, the former capital of the textile industry.
programme.desc-more: The North is a region that is particularly renowned for the warmth of its inhabitants. But this positive reputation is being undermined by many different acts and increasingly violent crime. In this border area, all kinds of traffic are spreading due to the proximity of the largest European ports. The magazine's team spent several weeks in the steps of the law enforcement forces that went to the front to stop the abuses of thugs, hunt the traffickers, appease the households or call the drivers, day and night.

programme.title: Hercules Poirot
programme.desc: "The Lost Mine" Poirot and Hastings play Monopoly. The game reminds the detective that he has to go to his bank to correct an error that occurred on his account.
programme.desc-more: Will Poirot ever be able to take a vacation? All his attempts were a baffling failure. First in the Cornwalls, where he plans to take the air with Hastings. Poirot's chivalry takes little rest, and they are soon to be thrown to the rescue of a young damsel in danger. In Whitcombe, after a busy London season, it is an antique flight that disturbs their serenity. Always quick to spread the mess in delicate affairs, and this despite all the good will of the world, Hastings does not lose anything of its comic potential. A pinch of humor welcome in the dreadful world of crime.

programme.desc-more: Is Poirot getting too old? Should he retire and cross his exciting career? Forget her taste for the investigation and get to seams? programme.title: Hunger Games: The Rebellion, Part One
programme.desc: Gathered by the rebels of District 13, Katniss, symbol of the revolt, is going to search for his friend Peeta, who was embezzled in the Capitol camp.
programme.desc-more: After cutting the bully of the Capitol to the ashes of the arena, Katniss Everdeen (Jennifer Lawrence) now embodies much more than just a survivor: she has become, despite herself, the face of a revolution. Exiled in District 13, a former underground military base headed by an iron hand by President Alma Coin, Katniss discovers a society organized for the war, where every decision could change Panem's destiny. But the young woman, marked by the trauma of the Games and the loss of those she loves, must overcome her own demons to take on this role. Advised by her closest allies – including Plutarch Heavensbee, a wise strategist, and Gale Hawthorne, her childhood friend – she is preparing to wage a much bigger battle than anything she has ever known. Its goal: to save Peeta Mellark, prisoner of the Capitol and victim of brainwashing, while uniting the districts under the same banner.

programme.title: Hunger Games: The Fire
programme.desc: After winning the 74th Hunger Games, Katniss Everdeen and his partner must return to the arena where the former winners are competing.
programme.desc-more: In a dystopic future where social inequalities have shaped a world divided into twelve districts oppressed by the Capitol, the Hunger Games remain a brutal reminder of the implacable authority of the regime. After their unexpected victory in the 74th edition, Katniss Everdeen (Jennifer Lawrence) and Peeta Mellark (Josh Hutcherson) became, despite them, the faces of silent resistance. Their act of final distrust in the arena, perceived as a gesture of love by the public but as a provocation by the power, sow the seeds of an dissatisfaction that now rumbles through Panem. As the two young men begin a Victory Tower imposed by the Capitol, each public appearance becomes a perilous exercise. In the spotlight, they must embody the image of a loving couple, a symbol of peace and submission, while President Snow (Donald Sutherland) observes, impassively, their slightest false step. But behind the flamboyant costumes designed by Cinna (Lenny Kravitz) and the forced smiles, Katniss feels pressure rising. The districts, once resigned, are beginning to see in it more than just a survivor: a spark of hope. Anodizing gestures – a three-finger greeting, a exchanged look – take on a subversive dimension, fuelling the anger of the Capitol. While Peeta, torn between her sincere love for Katniss and her loyalty to a system he has always known, tries to play the game, the young woman discovers the extent of the manipulations orchestrated by Snow. Haymitch Abernathy (Woody Harrelson), their disillusioned mentor, and Effie Trinket (Elizabeth Banks), their always impeccable but increasingly troubled escorts, become ambivalent allies in this deadly chess game. When Snow announces a special edition of the Hunger Games, bringing together former winners, Katniss understands that the trap is closing. The Capitol will no longer be content with symbols: it requires blood. Between the threat to his loved ones, fragile alliances with tributes like Finnick Odair (Sam Claflin) or Johanna Mason, and the revelation of secrets buried on the true nature of the rebellion, Katniss finds himself at the heart of a much larger conflict than games. Every decision could trigger an open war – or seal its destiny. In this world where survival is measured in strategies and sacrifices, a question persists: how far will it go to protect those whom it loves, and at what price?

programme.desc-more: In the bustling streets of New York, the Special Unit for Victims, led by the Olivia Benson (Mariska Hargitay) determined, is facing disturbing cases that test their skills and humanity. In this 21st season, inspectors, including the faithful Fin Tutuola (Ice-T) and the insight Kat Tamin (Jamie Gray Hyder), are delving into complex investigations of sexual crimes, child abuse and domestic violence. Unity, often confronted with failing systems and prejudices, must also manage its own internal struggles, while striving to restore hope and dignity to the people it serves. programme.desc: After gradually reducing his list of suspects concerning Red John, the serial killer who upset his life, Patrick Jane (Simon Baker) finds himself facing an increasingly complex dilemma. The closer he approaches the identity of the murderer, the more he intensifyes his acts of violence, sowing terror around him. Despite the traps set by Red John, Jane is perceptive and manages to expose the criminal. However, their explosive confrontation forces Jane to flee the country to escape the threat she faces. Two years later, Teresa Lisbon's team (Robin Tunney) was dissolved, and Van Pelt (Amanda Righetti) and Rigsby (Owain Yeoman) began a new life together. As Jane lives under a false identity, a new opportunity presents itself to him, marking the beginning of a season full of tensions and revelations, with the arrival of new characters, including Kim Fischer (Emily Swallow) and the FBI agent, who bring an unexpected dynamic to the plot.
programme.desc-more: Patrick Jane (Simon Baker), a talented mentalist who reads people and analyzes their behaviour, uses his skills to help the California Bureau of Investigation (CBI) solve complex criminal cases. With a sense of caustic humour and a sometimes controversial approach, he worked closely with Agent Teresa Lisbon (Robin Tunney), whose rigor and professionalism contrasted with Patrick's more disdainful nature. Together, they make up a dynamic team that navigates through thrilling investigations while trying to solve personal mysteries. In the background, Patrick is also obsessed with his quest for revenge against Red John, a serial killer who tragically took the life of his wife and daughter. This hunt led him to juggle his role as an investigator with his inner demons, revealing the depths of his psyche while unifying the sons of criminal plotters.

programme.title: Mentalist
programme.desc: In this captivating seventh season of Mindalist, Patrick Jane (Simon Baker), a former consultant for the California Bureau of Investigation, is teaming up with the FBI to solve a series of particularly complex homicides. After finally ending his personal quest for revenge against Red John, the famous serial killer, Patrick now focuses on new criminals, revealing unrivalled observation and deduction skills. Teresa Lisbon (Robin Tunney), now a permanent member of the FBI, is providing unwavering support to Patrick, strengthening their professional partnership while exploring the dynamics of their relationship. Together, they face cases that go beyond mere murders, plunged into intrigues of psychological manipulation and mind games. The challenges are increasing as characters with dark motivations enter the stage, and Patrick Jane has to navigate through a world of mysteries where nothing is ever really what it seems.

programme.title: One more smile: living with Down syndrome 21
programme.desc: For people with Down syndrome 21, inclusion is a daily struggle. Coline, 8, is preparing for her return to a regular school. Marie-Sarah and Florent live their love story in the open, despite the eyes of others. Arnaud took advantage of his success thanks to his role in the cinema, and Florian struggled to sign a CDI in an inclusive restaurant. Their loved ones are very sincere about the challenges and joys of their disability. Through their intimate and singular stories, discover their journeys, aspirations and ties with their entourage. The producers of the film "A little extra thing" reveal behind the scenes of the shooting through some anecdotes.

programme.title: 90' Investigations
programme.sub-title: Leaking: When new drivers take all the risks
programme.desc: The police are on the front line to fight against road offenders. For several years, behaviour has been increasing sharply, the crime of flight. Every twenty minutes in France, a driver tries to avoid a check. Unfortunately, these crazy strikes can be dramatic with sometimes fatal accidents. Evidence is used to understand why drivers take such risks and put other users at risk.

programme.title: Tattoo Cover : Tattoo Saviours
programme.desc: Dodie, Marty Early, Diego Moraes, Karina NG, considered one of the rising stars of old school tattoo, and Adrien, a Japanese style specialist, set up in a specially designed boutique in central Paris. These five tattoo virtuosos will take up a challenge: to remove shameful or completely missed tattoos by covering them with new creations. These five needle magicians are the last resort for desperate tattoos.

programme.title: TFou
programme.desc: Hello Kitty super style! ST / Ruben & cie ST / Paw Patrol, Pat'Patrouille ST / Robin des bois ST

programme.title: Baby boom
programme.desc: With the expert look of health professionals, an overview of the work of Bry-sur-Marne's maiuticians, all very committed to their profession.
programme.desc-more: The maternity of the private hospital of Marne-la-Vallée is celebrating its ten years. On this special occasion, the entire team – midwives, gynaecologists, nurses and child care workers – is gathered to celebrate the event. Among all this beautiful world, three men who are working as a Maeutician. As with their midwives, they are essential at the time of birth and are passionate about this profession, entirely dedicated to future mothers. And with nearly 2,000 births a year, there's a lot to do.

programme.title: Baby boom
programme.desc: For a year, the daily life and journey of several couples in desire for a child, engaged in the long journey of medically assisted reproduction.
programme.desc-more: Every year, no less than 750,000 babies are born in France. Many have been expected for a very long time and are the result of a long journey of LDCs (medically assisted human reproduction). These pregnancies are called precious pregnancies and are very special because medical presence was necessary for many months, even years before. The cameras followed Anna, a single mother from Cannes, Caroline and David, who live in Paris, Dihia and Mustapha, Rouen and finally Elise and Alice, a homoparental couple sailing between Barcelona and Lyon, all of whom have fought long to become parents.
